newsitem.title: USA: US wheat flour subsidies could target Yemen, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: US wheat flour subsidies could target Yemen, Egypt.

text.p: A decision to revive U.S. wheat flour export subsidies could have the biggest impact on sales to Yemen and Egypt, U.S. agriculture department and grain industry aides told Reuters.

Last week, U.S. Agriculture Department Secretary Dan Glickman confirmed that the United States was reviewing whether to revive U.S. wheat flour and barley malt export subsidies to help win back market share.
U.S. wheat flour exports have fallen from 710,900 tonnes in 1992/93 to just 162,500 in 1996/97, despite overall growth in world wheat flour trade.

U.S. wheat flour exports to Yemen peaked at 365,800 tonnes in 1994/95 (June-May), before falling to 130,200 in 1995/96 and to zero in 1996/97 in the face of increased competition from the European Union.
Yemen was the number one U.S. wheat flour market from 1993/94 through 1995/96. But last year, Mexico claimed that title with imports of just 60,000 tonnes from the U.S.
U.S. wheat flour shipments to Egypt have also fallen sharply, from 285,900 tonnes in 1992/93 to 8,000 in 1996/97.

A U.S. wheat flour industry aide, who asked not to be identified, blamed the lost U.S. sales on the Clinton administration's failure to respond to direct and indirect EU export subsidies over the past couple of years.
However, other analysts suggest that the EU's transportation cost advantage is the main factor behind its increased sales to the Middle East.
Tim Galvin, associate administrator of USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service said Monday that the Clinton administration's review of reviving wheat flour export subsidies is "moving along."
The deciding factor will be what action the EU takes in regard to wheat flour and barley malt subsidies, he said.
